title: European Commission hit by cyberattack affecting staff payroll and leave systems
date_note: Date of the report; Politico, relayed by Izvestia, says the attack had been going on for more than 10 days.
summary: Politico (relayed by Izvestia) reports an attack on the European Commission lasting over 10 days. Euronews quotes spokesman Thomas Regnier: first detected on 22 October, based on a publicly available AI tool, no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole. Sysper HR was unreachable for several days; JSIS insurance still down. Perpetrator and data theft unclear.
plain: The European Commission says some of its internal systems were attacked and some applications were switched off. Most staff were paid as usual, but some could not file time sheets or arrange leave.
exec: An attack on an EU institution's HR systems puts staff personal data at risk.
action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.
impact: HR systems affected: Sysper unavailable for several days, JSIS still unavailable per Euronews; possible exposure of staff data not established.

sources.name: The Telegraph via Yahoo News (relaying Politico)

validation.note: Euronews (own anonymous official; Sysper and JSIS named) and Politico (relayed by Izvestia, Telegraph, Anadolu, La Libre) report independently; the Commission has not confirmed the scope. Politico original not read.

review.note: Added Commission statement of no evidence of staff-wide data breach (Euronews); attributed 10+ days to Politico via Izvestia; Politico original unread
